work.geographic_association: Malan Tribe (Falangaw), Taitung; also linked to Northern Amis (Hualien) roots.

credited_creators.name: Lu Jingzi (盧靜子)
credited_creators.role: Primary songwriter/polisher and performer of the 1969 definitive version.

credited_creators.name: Traditional / Collective
credited_creators.role: Oral tradition roots within the Amis community.

work.thematic_content: A narrative song about a woman's unwavering love and resolve, famously featuring the line about lying on the 'kasolin' (train tracks). It is a significant marker of Amis matrilineal social dynamics and autonomy.

representative_recordings.notes: The most iconic indigenous recording, often cited as the reference for the modern Amis version.
Mandarin-language adaptation that popularized the melody in mainstream Taiwanese pop culture.
The earliest known audio documentation of the melody, recorded under the title '離別故鄉'.

representative_recordings.performer: Difang Duana (郭英男) & the Malan Singers
representative_recordings.notes: Highly influential international recording representing the polyphonic vocal style of the Malan Amis.

cultural_sensitivity_note: As a protected cultural expression of the Amis people, '馬蘭姑娘' should be handled with respect for its history of collective creation. Care should be taken to distinguish it from the 'Elders' Drinking Song' (part of the same Malan tradition but a distinct ancient chant).
